characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s, average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness after aging at 525 °C for 1 h = 562.3 ± 8.9 HV (compared with 263.8 ± 1.1 HV for the solution-treated 19Al baseline).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; specimen 10×5×2 mm³
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 1 h

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 525 °C the α matrix of the 19Al alloy remains almost featureless even after 10 h; the 525 °C/1 h panel shows a nearly featureless α matrix with faint grain boundaries and a 10 µm inset labelled α-Mn with twin-like lamellae.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging; 50 µm main-field scale bars, 10 µm insets (electrolytically polished samples, 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in the 19Al alloy after different aging treatments including 525 °C/1 h

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots of nominal Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 19) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated sample aged at 525 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching — this defines the terminal state of the current sample (19Al, 525 °C / 1 h).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness using an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 525 °C for 1 h the 19Al alloy remains essentially the single-phase α (BCC) matrix (with faint grain boundaries) inherited from the solution-treated state; precipitation of β-Mn is very slow at 525 °C, so essentially no resolved β-Mn network has developed at 1 h. Fine α-Mn particles (twin-like lamellae) are present within the α matrix.

unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy, β-Mn precipitation during low-temperature aging at 525 °C is very slow: even after 10 h of aging only a small amount of β-Mn (12.1 %) had precipitated, so at 1 h the microstructure remains essentially the untransformed α matrix containing fine α-Mn particles.

In the 19Al alloy the β-Mn precipitates primarily along α grain boundaries, with a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn also observed within the α grains; the α→β-Mn transformation was only completed after 10 h when aging at 550 °C, reflecting reduced β-Mn precipitation kinetics at higher Al content.
EDS-measured chemical composition of the 19Al alloy (Table 1): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (at.%).
The 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu) alloy density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.66 g·cm⁻³.
